chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no prayer for one who does not attend the obligatory prayers from among the residents of the mosque, when he is free and healthy."

key_terms.جِيرَانِ الْمَسْجِدِ: Residents of the mosque / Neighbors of the mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of prayer regarding attending congregational prayers for neighbors of the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes attending the congregational obligatory prayers as a condition for validity for those residing within the mosque's vicinity who are physically capable, highlighting the communal obligation of proximity. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the social dimension of worship, where the mosque serves as the center of community cohesion and religious discipline. The ruling underscores that while individual prayer is valid, the missed communal aspect diminishes the completeness of the act for those able to participate.
